ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a straight wire of length $L = 0.15\mathrm{m}$ carrying a current of $I = 2\mathrm{A}$. When this straight wire is placed perpendicular to the direction of a uniform magnetic field, the wire experiences an Ampere force of $F = 3.0 \times 10^{-2}\mathrm{N}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$ of this uniform magnetic field?
2. If the current in the wire is increased to $I' = 10\mathrm{A}$ while keeping other conditions unchanged, what is the magnitude of the Ampere force $F'$ acting on the conductor?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a straight wire of length $L = 0.15\mathrm{m}$ carrying a current of $I = 2\mathrm{A}$. When this straight wire is placed perpendicular to the direction of a uniform magnetic field, the wire experiences an Ampere force of $F = 3.0 \times 10^{-2}\mathrm{N}$. 1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$ of this uniform magnetic field? 2. If the current in the wire is increased to $I' = 10\mathrm{A}$ while keeping other conditions unchanged, what is the magnitude of the Ampere force $F'$ acting on the conductor?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given L = 0.15 m, I = 2 A, and F = 3.0×10^-2 N = 0.030 N. The wire is perpendicular to the magnetic field, so θ = 90° and sinθ = 1. Use the magnetic force law F = BIL sinθ, so B = F/(IL) = 0.030/(2×0.15) = 0.030/0.30 = 0.1 T. With B = 0.1 T and L = 0.15 m unchanged, when the current becomes I' = 10 A, the force is F' = BI'L = 0.1×10×0.15 = 0.15 N.
